G1017.name: Volt Typhoon
G1017.motive: Pre-position in critical infrastructure to enable disruption in a crisis.
G1017.blurb: PRC state-sponsored actor that lives off the land inside critical-infrastructure networks, often for years, and has been assessed as pre-positioning for disruptive action against OT.

traits.name: Pre-positioning
traits.text: Operates inside networks for long periods before acting: begins the battle with two hidden footholds.

traits.name: Living off the Land
traits.text: Prefers built-in tools (vssadmin, netsh, ntdsutil, wmic) over malware, so Execute and Stealth cards cost 1 less.

traits.name: Valid Accounts & Edge Devices
traits.text: Relies on valid credentials and internet-facing devices: its footholds start harder to see.

traits.name: Activation
traits.text: When its secrecy erodes it shifts from pre-positioning to disruption and gains +1 energy.

G1017.note: Destructive impact is an *assessed intent* (CISA AA24-038A), not an observed technique — its Strike card is marked as such.

G0034.name: Sandworm Team
G0034.motive: Disruption and destruction in support of Russian state objectives.
G0034.blurb: GRU-linked actor responsible for the Ukrainian grid attacks, NotPetya and numerous destructive operations; combines supply-chain access, valid accounts and wipers.

traits.name: State Resources
traits.text: Well-resourced and patient: +1 energy each turn.

traits.name: Escalation to Destruction
traits.text: From round 5 its Strike and Impair cards gain +1 power.

traits.name: Trusted Relationships
traits.text: Abuses supply-chain and vendor trust: starts with one hidden foothold.

G0016.name: APT29
G0016.blurb: SVR-linked actor known for SolarWinds, extensive cloud and identity abuse, and exceptional operational security.

traits.name: Operational Security
traits.text: Exceptional tradecraft: its footholds start with +2 stealth.

traits.name: Identity Abuse
traits.text: Targets identity and cloud tokens: ignores 1 Authentication ward.

traits.name: Strategic Collection
traits.text: Gameplay trait: data it exfiltrates from assets without post-quantum protection becomes “quantum debt” — future decryption risk that costs Resilience after the battle.
traits.note: Illustrates the general harvest-now-decrypt-later risk for strategic collectors; not an APT29-specific finding.

G0032.name: Lazarus Group
G0032.motive: Revenue generation and espionage for the DPRK regime.
G0032.blurb: DPRK-linked group behind destructive attacks, large-scale cryptocurrency theft and long-running social-engineering campaigns such as Operation Dream Job.

traits.name: Targeted Lures
traits.text: Convincing social engineering: ignores 1 Authentication ward.

traits.name: Revenue Pressure
traits.text: From round 4 its Strike cards gain +1 power.

traits.name: Dual Mission
traits.text: Draws one extra card per turn.

G0096.name: APT41
G0096.motive: State espionage alongside financially motivated intrusions.
G0096.blurb: Chinese state-sponsored actor that also conducts financially motivated operations; known for supply-chain compromise and rapid exploitation of internet-facing software.

traits.name: Rapid Exploitation
traits.text: Breach cards cost 1 less: quick to weaponise public flaws.

traits.name: Dual Mission
traits.text: Draws one extra card per turn.

G0007.name: APT28
G0007.blurb: GRU-linked actor known for credential harvesting, password spraying and exploiting edge devices.

G0045.name: menuPass
G0045.motive: Intellectual-property theft by compromising managed service providers.
G0045.blurb: Chinese state-linked actor known for “Operation Cloud Hopper”: compromising managed service providers to reach their customers’ networks.

traits.name: Trusted Relationship
traits.text: Reaches victims through their service providers: begins with one hidden foothold.

G0129.name: Mustang Panda
G0129.motive: Intelligence collection, often via USB and phishing lures.
G0129.blurb: PRC-linked actor with a large toolset and broad targeting, frequently using phishing and removable-media propagation.

traits.name: Large Toolset
traits.text: Draws one extra card per turn.

G0046.name: FIN7
G0046.blurb: Financially motivated group known for phishing, point-of-sale malware and later ransomware affiliations.

G0102.name: Wizard Spider
G0102.blurb: Cybercriminal group behind TrickBot, Ryuk and Conti: human-operated ransomware against large organisations.

traits.name: Big-Game Hunting
traits.text: From round 5 its Strike cards gain +1 power.

G1015.name: Scattered Spider
G1015.blurb: Native-English-speaking group that social-engineers help desks, abuses MFA fatigue and SIM swapping, then pivots through cloud and SaaS.

G0035.name: Dragonfly
G0035.blurb: Long-running actor targeting energy and industrial organisations, using trusted-relationship and watering-hole access.

G0117.name: Fox Kitten
G0117.motive: Access via VPN and edge-device exploitation.
G0117.blurb: Iran-linked actor that exploits VPN and other edge appliances to gain and sell access.

G0082.name: APT38
G0082.motive: Theft from banks via payment systems.
G0082.blurb: DPRK-linked group targeting banks and SWIFT-connected payment infrastructure.

G1057.name: ShinyHunters
G1057.motive: Data theft and extortion from SaaS and cloud platforms.
G1057.blurb: Data-extortion crew that abuses stolen credentials and OAuth/API access to bulk-export SaaS data.

traits.name: SaaS Bulk Export
traits.text: Collection and Exfiltration cards cost 1 less.

G0125.name: HAFNIUM
G0125.motive: Exploit public-facing servers for data theft.
G0125.blurb: State-sponsored actor that exploited zero-days in on-premises Exchange servers at scale.

traits.name: Zero-Day Exploitation
traits.text: Breach cards cost 1 less and footholds start with +1 stealth.

G0114.name: Chimera
G0114.motive: Theft of semiconductor and aviation IP.
G0114.blurb: Actor known for patient, targeted intrusions against technology firms using stolen credentials and Cobalt Strike.

G0049.name: OilRig
G0049.blurb: Iran-linked actor with a broad toolset and heavy use of spearphishing and credential theft.

traits.name: Broad Toolset
traits.text: Draws one extra card per turn.

G0088.name: TEMP.Veles
G0088.blurb: Actor associated with the Triton/Trisis malware targeting safety instrumented systems at an industrial facility.

traits.name: Safety-System Focus
traits.text: Inhibit and Impair cards cost 1 less.

G0139.name: TeamTNT
G0139.motive: Cloud and container compromise for cryptomining.
G0139.blurb: Cloud-focused group that exploits exposed Docker/Kubernetes and steals cloud credentials to run cryptominers.

G0106.name: Rocke
G0106.blurb: Cryptojacking group that exploits unpatched public-facing services and persists with cron jobs.

G0092.name: TA505
G0092.motive: Mass phishing, banking malware and ransomware affiliations.
G0092.blurb: Financially motivated actor known for large-scale phishing campaigns and distribution of banking trojans and ransomware.

traits.name: Mass Campaigns
traits.text: Draws one extra card per turn.

G0037.name: FIN6
G0037.motive: Payment-card theft from retail and hospitality.
G0037.blurb: Financially motivated actor that compromises point-of-sale systems to steal card data.

G0091.name: Silence
G0091.motive: Theft from banks via payment and ATM systems.
G0091.blurb: Financially motivated group targeting banks in Eastern Europe and beyond.

G0080.name: Cobalt Group
G0080.blurb: Financially motivated group known for ATM jackpotting and bank intrusions using Cobalt Strike.

traits.name: Cash-Out Focus
traits.text: Exfiltration cards gain +1 power from round 3.

G1004.name: LAPSUS$
G1004.motive: Data theft and extortion; recruits insiders.
G1004.blurb: Extortion group known for social engineering, SIM swapping and recruiting insiders to obtain access.

G1051.name: Medusa Group
G1051.blurb: Ransomware operation with a data-leak site and an affiliate model.

traits.name: Double Extortion
traits.text: From round 4 its Strike cards gain +1 power.

G1043.name: BlackByte
G1043.blurb: Ransomware group that exploits public-facing services and abuses legitimate tooling.

G1032.name: INC Ransom
G1032.blurb: Ransomware operation using valid accounts and legitimate remote tools.

C0025.name: 2016 Ukraine Electric Power Attack
C0025.blurb: Documented December 2016 attack on Ukrainian electric power: Industroyer-style manipulation of substation protocols.

C0028.name: 2015 Ukraine Electric Power Attack
C0028.blurb: Documented December 2015 attack on Ukrainian distribution utilities: remote HMI control and breaker opening.

C0030.name: Triton Safety Instrumented System Attack
C0030.blurb: Documented 2017 attack that compromised a safety instrumented system at an industrial plant.

C0024.name: SolarWinds Compromise
C0024.blurb: SolarWinds Compromise (2019–2021): a software supply-chain intrusion that enabled access to many downstream victims.

C0034.name: 2022 Ukraine Electric Power Attack
C0034.blurb: Documented 2022 attack on Ukrainian electric power using Industroyer2 and wipers.

traits.name: Destructive Payload
traits.text: From round 5 its Strike cards gain +1 power.

C0063.name: 2025 Poland Wiper Attacks
C0063.blurb: Documented 2025 wiper attacks against Polish organisations.

traits.name: Destructive Payload
traits.text: From round 4 its Strike cards gain +1 power.

C0057.name: 3CX Supply Chain Attack
C0057.blurb: 3CX supply-chain attack (2022–2023): a trojanised desktop application used to reach downstream victims.

C0029.name: Cutting Edge
C0029.blurb: Cutting Edge: exploitation of edge-device zero-days (Ivanti) in 2023–2024.

C0012.name: Operation CuckooBees
C0012.blurb: Operation CuckooBees: long-running theft of intellectual property from technology and manufacturing firms.

C0059.name: Salesforce Data Exfiltration
C0059.blurb: Salesforce data exfiltration: extortion following bulk export from SaaS tenants.

traits.name: SaaS Bulk Export
traits.text: Collection and Exfiltration cards cost 1 less.

C0058.name: SharePoint ToolShell Exploitation
C0058.blurb: SharePoint ToolShell exploitation (2025): remote code execution against on-premises SharePoint.

C0020.name: Maroochy Water Breach
C0020.blurb: Maroochy Water Breach (2000): an insider used radio-controlled equipment to release sewage in Queensland — an Australian ICS case study.

C0049.name: Leviathan Australian Intrusions
C0049.blurb: Leviathan Australian Intrusions (2022): a documented campaign against Australian targets.

C0014.name: Operation Wocao
C0014.blurb: Operation Wocao (2017–2019): wide-ranging intrusions using legitimate tools and credentials.

C0041.name: FrostyGoop Incident
C0041.blurb: FrostyGoop incident (2024): ICS malware manipulating Modbus on heating controllers.

C0022.name: Operation Dream Job
C0022.blurb: Operation Dream Job: fake job offers used to deliver malware and steal data and cryptocurrency.
